events.summary: Round-1's two decisive objections are now resolved by direct measurement, and the causal chain is grounded end to end. (1) TEMPORAL ORDER: my round-1 inversion is gone. At 1-min resolution the gateway p99, gateway 5xx and portfolio-service p99 all show a clean single step at the 09:53:00Z bucket (09:51/09:52 flat at baseline), so the earlier 09:45/09:51 "degraded buckets" were 3-min boundary artifacts (F13/F14/F15). The measured ordering is now: cfg-2207 applied 09:52:13Z (F17, in-log) -> db_pool_in_use drops to 8.45 then pins at exactly 5.0 from 09:53 (F16/F25) -> first HikariCP acquire error 09:53:19Z (F17/F27) -> first gateway 504 at 09:53:53Z, i.e. the upstream failure precedes the gateway symptom by 34s (F9/F18). Cause precedes onset tightly for the first time. (2) THE LOAD-BEARING HOP IS NOW MEASURED, not assumed: the pool is pinned at exactly the new 5-connection ceiling with zero variance (F16/F25), HikariCP logs give total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=25-57 (F18/F27) — a size-induced starvation signature, not a slow-store signature — while request_rate holds ~550-580 rps and CPU ~36% straight through onset (F29), killing load/CPU explanations. H4 (load surge) is correctly rejected on F29/F26. H2 (envoy/HTTP/2 deploy at 08:00Z) is now affirmatively contradicted, not merely unsupported: the pool sat stable at ~11.6-12.3 from 07:45 to 09:51 with flat load (F26), so the deploy produced no portfolio-path effect for ~113 min and the onset tracks the 09:52 config change, not the deploy; gateway CPU/mem stay flat (F11) and the error signature is a held-open upstream timeout with an upstream acquire error that precedes it (F9/F17/F18). H3 (shared store) is the only remaining live alternative, and it is not dismissed on connection to the path (ledger-db/redis-cache are shared and on the path, F19/F20/F21) but on the shape of the evidence: the failure is acquire-queue starvation against a pool pinned at exactly the newly-lowered ceiling, with no headroom metric exceeding 5 even once, which a slow store cannot produce; and no deployment touched either store (F23), with cfg-2207 the only never-reverted change (F22) and gateway v9.3.0 the only other live change (F24). Residual uncertainty is real but secondary, so I cap at 0.85 rather than higher: (a) H3 is untested by direct ledger-db/redis-cache metrics, and (b) the pre-change Hikari total=50 was never observed in a log line (the ceiling is inferred from the metric plateau plus log total=5). Neither could plausibly reorder the hypotheses: a slow shared store would still have to explain a pool pinned at exactly 5.0 with request volume and CPU flat, and would produce slow queries rather than an acquire queue. Remaining tool budget is better spent on mitigation (revert/raise cfg-2207) than on confirmation queries.

(2) THE LOAD-BEARING HOP IS NOW MEASURED, not assumed: the pool is pinned at exactly the new 5-connection ceiling with zero variance (F16/F25), HikariCP logs give total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=25-57 (F18/F27) — a size-induced starvation signature, not a slow-store signature — while request_rate holds ~550-580 rps and CPU ~36% straight through onset (F29), killing load/CPU explanations. H2 (envoy/HTTP/2 deploy at 08:00Z) is now affirmatively contradicted, not merely unsupported: the pool sat stable at ~11.6-12.3 from 07:45 to 09:51 with flat load (F26), so the deploy produced no portfolio-path effect for ~113 min and the onset tracks the 09:52 config change, not the deploy; gateway CPU/mem stay flat (F11) and the error signature is a held-open upstream timeout with an upstream acquire error that precedes it (F9/F17/F18). Remaining tool budget is better spent on mitigation (revert/raise cfg-2207) than on confirmation queries.
